pages.text:
BIRD TO THE COMPUTER

The next page holds a bird
to the workshop’s own
machine. Take her off the
page and give her one of
the letters that follow;
the answer comes back to
her nest as a number or a
box.

Every letter needs a bird
in its last hole to answer
to: put one of yours there.

THE TIME

[query | time | bird]

answers with the clock: the
milliseconds since the
workshop opened, as one
number. A thousand a second.

Ask twice and take the
difference: that is how long
something took.

THE DATE

[query | date | bird]

answers with a box of three
numbers: [year | month | day].

Take the year out of the
first hole and it is a
number like any other.

THE CLOCK

[query | clock | bird]

answers with a box of three
numbers:
[hours | minutes | seconds].

A TIMER, FROM ROBOTS

A number can be TOLD its
value: give its bird
[set | value | n].

So a timer is a robot that
asks the computer the time,
tells its number the answer,
and asks again. The world
timer.world.json in this
folder is that robot, bound
to a number on the table.

thing.text:
THE COMPUTER

This notebook holds a bird
to the workshop’s own
machine, and the letters it
answers. Point at the
notebook and press the left
and right arrows to turn
its pages; click a page to
take a copy of what is on
it.
